title: dar in the dot past (di, dio), le lo → se lo, clarifying with a él / a ella

cards.title: dar acts like -er/-ir: di, dio, dimos
cards.body: The only verb that switches sides like this in the dot past.

examples.en: He didn't give it to us.

cards.title: First thought: who's doing it
cards.body: Start with 'I gave' (di); the rest flows from there.

cards.title: le lo → se lo (a sound change)
cards.body: Spanish avoids two l-words together: le lo / les lo / le los become se lo / se los. It's purely about sound, not the 'self' se.

examples.en: I gave it to him / her / them / you all.

cards.title: Clarify by adding a él / a ella
cards.body: Keep the whole sentence and add a + person at the end, repeating rather than restructuring.

examples.es: Le di algo a él. / Le di algo a ella.

cards.title: a repeats; para doesn't
cards.body: With a, the little word stays (me lo compra a mí: for me or from me). With para, there's no repetition (lo compra para mí).

cards.title: se lo envió + clarifications
cards.body: A fixed core (se lo envió) with clarifications around it.

examples.en: He hasn't sent it to you guys yet.
examples.es: No se lo envió a ustedes todavía.

examples.en: I don't know if I sent it to him.
examples.es: No sé si se lo envié.

cards.title: Understand, don't memorise
cards.body: Fine details like this will come back through active listening and analysis.

practice.en: I sold them (feminine things) to her.

es: Él se lo envió a ella

practice.en: He hasn't sent it to you guys yet.
es: No se lo envió a ustedes todavía
No se lo envió todavía a ustedes
Todavía no se lo envió a ustedes
